title: D3D12: long main-thread stalls allocating many small buffers (D3D12MA TLSF search checks every free block)
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable (bundled D3D12MA 3.1.0).
- The same code is in `master` (befe24c) and in upstream D3D12MemoryAllocator 3.2.0.

### System information

Windows 11 (10.0.26200), D3D12 Forward+, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070, NVIDIA driver 617.14, Agility SDK 1.618 (tight alignment active).

### Issue description

When a game streams in world sections, each one creates a few thousand small storage buffers (MultiMesh instance data, averaging about 1.4 KB). On D3D12 this stalls the main thread at the streaming boundaries, with boundary frames of up to 4 s; the patch below cut the worst to 1.3 s. Main-thread stack samples taken during the stalls are in `BlockMetadata_TLSF::CreateAllocationRequest` → `CheckBlock`, in the "Worst case, full search" loop.

Cause: `nextListIndex` starts at 0. If `FindFreeBlock(sizeForNextList, nextListIndex)` finds nothing, it returns `NULL` without writing `nextListIndex`. The worst-case loop then calls `CheckBlock` on every free block in lists 1 and up. Every block in the lists below `allocSize`'s list is smaller than the request, so all of those checks fail. `BlockVector::AllocatePage` tries each existing heap in turn, so a single allocation can walk every free fragment in every heap. We think tight alignment makes this worse: small buffers are packed at 128 B, so freed buffers leave many small fragments (not measured).

Change: when `nextListIndex` is still 0, start the loop at `allocSize`'s list. No allocation result changes: every skipped block fails `CheckBlock`, which has no side effect on failure. A seeded alloc/free replay through both versions gives identical offsets for all three strategies (default, `MIN_TIME`, `MIN_MEMORY`). The patch adds 9 lines in `thirdparty/d3d12ma/D3D12MemAlloc.cpp` (diff below; a PR would also add it as `patches/0002-tlsf-worst-case-start.patch` per `thirdparty/README.md`). Godot's bundled VMA skips this loop entirely when no larger block exists (`nextListIndex = m_ListsCount`); that form should also give identical results. This patch is the more conservative change.

```diff
     // Worst case, full search has to be done
+    // nextListIndex is still 0 when no free block of sizeForNextList or larger was found.
+    // Lists below allocSize's list hold only smaller blocks, which CheckBlock always rejects,
+    // so start at allocSize's list instead of checking every free block in the heap.
+    if (nextListIndex == 0)
+    {
+        const UINT32 sizeListIndex = GetListIndex(allocSize);
+        if (sizeListIndex > 0)
+            nextListIndex = sizeListIndex - 1;
+    }
     while (++nextListIndex < m_ListsCount)
```

Results: same replay, same route, same build apart from the patch, one run each.

| | Unpatched | Patched |
|---|---|---|
| Spike frame time, sum | 25,032 ms | 14,165 ms (−43%) |
| Worst spike | 4,189 ms | 1,345 ms |
| Stall-watch events with the main thread in the full-scan loop | 5 | 0 |

Preliminary: one replay each, not soak-tested. The search is shorter but not gone. With the patch, `CreateAllocationRequest` still accounts for 27–57% of the samples in the slowest boundary frames.

I'm happy to open the PR here, upstream to D3D12MemoryAllocator, or both, whichever you prefer.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a few thousand small storage buffers per frame, for example many `MultiMesh` resources with small instance counts. Free and recreate them in batches so the D3D12MA heaps fragment. Then profile the main thread around the batch.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Not attached yet.
